content: Plan r1 for Phase 8 open-pr (B2 of the Aegis Bugalizer arc): docs/phases/open-pr.md, staged on branch phase-8/open-pr (based on docs/phase-7-complete, PR #4, which merges first). One endpoint, POST /reports/{id}/open-pr, turns a fix_proposed report into a GitHub PR: fetch, throwaway git worktree off origin/<default_branch> (analysis clone untouched), strict git apply --check then apply, branch fix/bugalizer-<report-id>, commit, look up an existing PR (DB then GitHub by head ref), push without force, open a non-draft PR with the analysis as the body, record pr_url/pr_number/pushed_sha. State: fix_proposed -> fix_approved (CAS claim) -> fix_committed; new rollback edge fix_approved -> fix_proposed on failure; both states stay out of CURRENT_PHASE_TARGETS so PATCH /status cannot enter them. Token BUGALIZER_GITHUB_TOKEN (fine-grained, spherop/sonicgrid only) reaches git only via GIT_CONFIG_* env extraheader, never URL/argv/config/log/response. Greg's rulings taken 2026-09-17: R1 single fine-grained token in service env, R2 a stale diff returns 409 diff_does_not_apply and never re-analyzes, R3 worktree not the analysis clone. 11 success criteria incl. real-git tests against a local bare repo with a mocked GitHub REST client, argv no-force assertion, concurrency, secrecy sentinel on every failure path, and Greg's BOWIE acceptance via scripts/windows/open-pr-smoke.ps1. Roadmap: Phase 8 entry added, Phase 6 B2 bullet points at it. No code yet; no tests run for plan review.

Plan review: REQUEST_CHANGES. R1 (service token), R2 (no re-analysis on stale diff), and R3 (isolated worktree) are preserved. No unconsumed interjections were present. Reviewed the plan, roadmap diff, and existing git/CAS/proposal code; no tests run for this plan-only submission.

1. Crash recovery cannot reach the promised reconciliation (docs/phases/open-pr.md, steps 2 and 7; success criterion 2). A process death after claiming leaves the persisted report at fix_approved, so the next request fails the CAS before looking up an existing GitHub PR. A crash can also leave the worktree directory present; prune does not remove an existing worktree. Specify safe abandoned-claim recovery, distinguishing an active request from a dead owner, and recovery/cleanup of its scratch worktree. Reconcile an existing PR before requiring the old diff to apply or constructing a new commit: an already merged PR may make that diff fail on the new base. Define atomic persistence of the PR record and final report state. Add restart tests at claim, PR-created-before-DB-write, and finalization boundaries, asserting the same PR is returned without another push or POST.

2. Ordinary retries retain a conflicting local branch (steps 6 and 11). git switch -c creates a branch in the shared repository; worktree removal/prune does not delete that branch. After a push/API failure and the specified rollback, the next request fails at switch -c before it can even discover a PR. Specify either detached commits with an explicit destination ref or safe ownership-aware local branch cleanup/reuse. Add a real-git failure-then-retry test on the same clone, without manually deleting local refs between requests. Preserve the stated no-overwrite policy for an existing remote branch with no PR; explicitly document the resulting recovery action when push succeeds but PR creation fails.

3. Make the authenticated remote commands agree with the HTTPS policy (steps 3, 4, 8 and Token handling). The plan promises https://github.com/o/r.git regardless of clone transport, but push origin uses the existing origin, which may be SSH (explicitly accepted); the HTTP extraheader cannot authenticate that push. Fetch also gets no token, so a private HTTPS clone cannot rely on the configured service token for this operation. Specify a validated canonical HTTPS destination for fetch/ls-remote/push, scoped credentials for every required authenticated operation, and how the fetched SHA is selected for the worktree without changing the analysis clone's persistent remote configuration. Test an SSH-origin clone and an HTTPS private-repo authentication path, including destination and credential assertions.

4. State report-wide idempotency and proposal ownership explicitly (Scope 1 and step 1). The current lookup checks the selected/newest proposal for pr_url, although the API promises one PR per report. If an older explicitly selected proposal opened the PR, a default repeat selects a different proposal and falls through to wrong_status. Look up the report's recorded PR across its proposals before default selection, and require any supplied fix_proposal_id to belong to the requested report before any mutation. Specify missing/foreign proposal responses and add tests for an older proposal followed by a bodyless repeat, a repeat selecting another proposal, and a foreign report's proposal ID.

Plan r2 for open-pr: docs/phases/open-pr.md revised (staged), addressing all four r1 findings. R1/R2/R3 unchanged. There were no unconsumed interjections. Plan-only, so no tests were run.

1. Crash recovery (Scope 3, steps 3/4/5/10, SC3). The claim now writes a per-request `bug_reports.claim_token`, and an in-process registry holds the live tokens. A `fix_approved` report whose token is not in the registry is abandoned: its owner process died or its rollback write failed. This relies on the already-documented single-process design, which is now in the decision log and Risks. The next request adopts the claim with a CAS on the observed token; a live token gets 409 `in_progress`. Step 4 cleans up leftovers keyed by report id: worktree remove --force, prune, rm of the dir (path asserted under `<repos_dir>/.worktrees/`), and the private base ref. Step 5 reconciles with GitHub (PR by head, state=all) BEFORE any apply or commit, so an already-merged PR returns 200 even if the diff no longer applies. Step 10 is one SQLite transaction (`record_pull_request`): it writes the proposal PR fields and moves the report fix_approved->fix_committed via a CAS on its own token, all-or-nothing. SC3 restart tests: (a) crash after claim with leftover worktree, (b) PR created before the DB write, (b') same but PR merged and base moved, (c) injected failure at finalization plus the committed case, and a live-claim in_progress case. Each asserts push/POST counts.

2. Local branch conflicts (Scope 2, steps 8/9, SC4, Risks). No local branch is ever created: the commit is built detached and pushed as `HEAD:refs/heads/fix/bugalizer-<id>`. The push intent (`pushed_sha`) is recorded before the push. On a retry, a remote branch whose tip equals a recorded `pushed_sha` for this report resumes at the PR POST with no push. Any other tip gives `branch_exists`, untouched; the manual recovery (open the PR by hand, which step 5 then finds, or delete the branch) is documented in Risks and deploy-windows.md. SC4 covers failure-then-retry on the same clone with no manual ref cleanup: PR POST 500 then resume (0 push, 1 POST), and push rejected then fixed. It asserts the branch list is unchanged and no refs/bugalizer/* or worktrees are left.

3. HTTPS/credentials (step 2, step 6, Token and remote handling, SC7). Every remote command (ls-remote, fetch, push) uses the validated canonical `<github_web_base>/o/r.git` as an explicit argv destination and never `origin`, so the clone's transport and config are irrelevant and never changed. All three get the env-only extraheader, empty credential.helper and GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0. The base is fetched into a private non-forced ref `refs/bugalizer/base/<id>` and resolved to a SHA for `worktree add --detach`, so remote-tracking refs and FETCH_HEAD are not touched. SC7: an SSH-origin clone still succeeds with the canonical destination in every argv; a real auth path goes through a local `git http-backend` server that 401s without the header, with a control run proving enforcement; env credential assertions on every remote call; `.git/config` byte-identical.

4. Report-wide idempotency and ownership (Scope 1, step 1, SC2). The order is: report 404; a supplied proposal must belong to this report, else 404 `proposal_not_found` (same response for unknown and foreign); then a report-wide recorded-PR lookup across all proposals, before default selection. A bodyless call or the same proposal -> 200 with the owning `fix_proposal_id`; a different proposal -> 409 `pr_exists`. All of this happens before any mutation. SC2 tests the older-proposal-then-bodyless repeat, a repeat naming the other proposal, and foreign/unknown IDs with unchanged state.

Plan review: REQUEST_CHANGES. The revised detached-commit retry path, canonical authenticated destinations, token-aware claim recovery under the stated single-process assumption, and atomic finalization address most of r1. R1/R2/R3 remain preserved. No unconsumed interjections were present. Reviewed the revised plan, roadmap diff, existing git/proposal code, and local git fetch help; no tests run for this plan-only submission.

1. Preserve proposal ownership during GitHub reconciliation (Technical Approach steps 1, 5 and 10; SC2/SC3). Step 5's PR-found branch finalizes before the pushed_sha-to-proposal lookup used in its no-PR branch. With older proposal A explicitly selected, a crash after PR creation but before finalization leaves no pr_url in the DB. A bodyless retry selects newest proposal B, finds A's PR, and the specified sequence records that PR against B. The same issue occurs when the retry explicitly names B. Specify how reconciliation resolves the PR's original proposal from durable push intent/operation metadata before finalization, including the closed/merged case, and return the owning proposal for a bodyless retry or pr_exists for an explicitly different proposal. Define the behavior when ownership cannot be established (including the documented manually opened PR recovery), rather than silently attributing it to the current default. Extend the restart tests with two proposals: A opens the PR, crash before DB finalization, then bodyless and explicit-B retries. Assert only A receives PR fields, the response identifies A, and neither retry pushes or POSTs.

2. Correct the concrete fetch command in step 6. A private destination ref does not prevent git fetch from writing FETCH_HEAD; the listed command omits --no-write-fetch-head despite promising that FETCH_HEAD consumers are untouched. Add that flag and a real-git isolation assertion preserving a pre-existing FETCH_HEAD byte-for-byte through success and failure paths. The local git fetch help confirms this option is available.

Plan r3 for open-pr: docs/phases/open-pr.md revised (staged). It addresses both r2 findings. R1/R2/R3 are unchanged. There were no unconsumed interjections. This is plan-only, so no tests were run.

1. Proposal ownership during reconciliation (Revision r3 note; Scope 1 outcomes; steps 5, 8 and 10; SC3 d/e/f; Risks). When step 5 finds a PR, it resolves the owning proposal from durable data before any write, and never from the request's selection:
   (i) the proposal whose recorded `pushed_sha` equals the PR's `head.sha` or appears in `GET /pulls/<n>/commits`. At most one proposal can match, because each commit's message names its proposal;
   (ii) otherwise, the `Bugalizer-Proposal:` + `Bugalizer-Report:` commit trailers, which step 8 now writes. These cover a lost intent write;
   (iii) otherwise the PR is unattributed. With a caller-named proposal, that explicit choice is the attribution; this is the documented manual recovery. Without one, the call returns `409 pr_unattributed {pr_url, pr_number}`, records nothing, and rolls back.
   The GitHub API keeps commits and PR state for closed and merged PRs, so no branch fetch is needed. `record_pull_request(report_id, proposal_id, ...)` writes only the owner's row and asserts that the owner belongs to the report. The response follows the Scope-1 rule: 200 with the owner's `fix_proposal_id` for a bodyless or owner-named call, or `409 pr_exists` naming the owner for a different proposal. The PR is still recorded against the owner in that case, so a later DB lookup gives the same answer.
   Tests:
   - SC3(d): A opens the PR, then a crash before finalization; separate bodyless and explicit-B runs. Only A gets PR fields, B's row is byte-identical, the response names A (200 or pr_exists), and there are 0 pushes and 0 POSTs. Both runs are repeated with the PR merged and the base moved.
   - SC3(e): intent lost, owner found through the trailers.
   - SC3(f): a hand-opened, trailer-less PR returns 409 pr_unattributed with no writes; then naming B records it against B with 0 pushes and 0 POSTs.

2. FETCH_HEAD (step 6, SC10). The fetch is now `git fetch --no-tags --no-write-fetch-head <canonical> refs/heads/<default>:refs/bugalizer/base/<id>`. Git 2.29 or later is required: deploy-windows.md states it, and an older git gets a clear 502 with no fallback. SC10 adds a pre-existing FETCH_HEAD, byte-identical after the happy, stale-diff, push-failure and fetch-failure paths, plus an argv assertion that every fetch carries the flag.

Approved. Reviewed docs/phases/open-pr.md, the roadmap diff, and the round-3 submission against the prior findings. Reconciliation now resolves the original proposal before atomic finalization, preserves ownership on bodyless and explicit-other-proposal retries, and defines explicit attribution for manually opened PRs whose owner cannot be established. The planned two-proposal restart tests cover open and merged PRs without another push or POST. The fetch now includes --no-write-fetch-head, with isolation assertions on success and failure paths. Both round-2 findings are addressed; the earlier recovery, detached-commit, authenticated-destination, and report-wide idempotency requirements remain intact. R1/R2/R3 are preserved. No unconsumed interjections were present. No tests run for this plan-only review. Proceed to implementation and its specified verification; BOWIE acceptance remains Greg's post-merge step.
